title: Manchester United's Pochettino Plan Hinges on Carrick's Future
body:
Manchester United have reportedly agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal to bring in Mauricio Pochettino as head coach [S1]. The club are reportedly close to a deal with Pochettino if they decide to sack Carrick [S2].

The timing is awkward. Carrick was still reporting for work while the Pochettino talks were moving [S2]. Sky Sports ran both versions, one saying the agreement was done and one saying it depended on a sacking [S1][S2]. That gap is the real story. The decision is being made in public before it has been fully made in private.

The results explain the nerves. They have scored 6 and conceded 11 [ST1], and the run reads DDLLD [ST1]. That is a side that has stopped winning and started leaking goals, and a manager change is the kind of move that gets pulled out when things turn ugly.

Every board loves a fresh start, but supporters just want a plan that survives a bad month. The sack is the easiest lever to pull and the hardest to pull well. A new coach with a long contract only helps if the structure around him can handle the next poor run, not just the headlines around the appointment.

The Touchline Take: get the next appointment right and this whole mess gets forgotten, but get it wrong and the dugout becomes the story all season.
